newsitem.title: USA: AOL reports third-quarter profit, marketing costs drop.
newsitem.headline: AOL reports third-quarter profit, marketing costs drop.

text.p: America Online Inc. reported a $2.6 million third-quarter profit that represented a big drop from a year ago but beat analysts' forecast for a loss as the world's largest online service was helped by lower marketing expenses.

America Online said net income for its fiscal third quarter ended March 31 equalled 2 cents a share and represented an 83 percent fall from $15.13 million, or 14 cents a share, in the year-ago quarter.
But Wall Street analysts on average had predicted a loss of 7 cents a share for the latest quarter, according to the First Call service.
America Online said that, as planned, it held its membership relatively flat at about 8 million subscribers while it worked to improve access for existing members.

When the Dulles, Va.-based company launched flat-rate, unlimited-access pricing in December, a surge in demand resulted in network access problems, angering subscribers who kept getting busy signals when they tried to log on.
America Online's revenues climbed to a record $456.2 million, up 46 percent from $312.3 million a year ago.

Non-subscription revenues grew to $74.7 million, including advertising and electronic commerce revenues of $60.7 million which represented a 37 percent increase from the previous quarter, the company said. America Online has said it would seek to raise the proportion of revenues coming from ads and commerce vs. subscription fees.

AOL said that during the quarter, it signed up 27 new advertisers, despite it being a seasonally slow period for advertising. The company said it now has more than 180 advertising clients, including companies such as Barnes & Noble Inc., American Greetings and TRW Inc.

The company also said that, as expected, member cancellations increased in January, due to the change in flat-rate pricing and access issues. But it also said member retention improved steadily as the quarter progressed.
America Online said the rates of conversion of trial memberships to full memberships and membership retention for April hit their highest levels for the past year.
It said it recently resumed marketing on a limited basis and plans to continue carefully balancing demand for the service with its ability to continue improving access.
When its members started experiencing major problems in January in accessing the system, America Online announced a $350 million programme to expand its network.
"As promised, we have worked around the clock to serve our existing members first and our top priority was, and still is, improving access," said company Chairman Steve Case.
"At the same time, we have achieved profitability a bit ahead of schedule," Case said in a statement.
America Online said that as part of its system expansion programme, it has installed more than 75,000 new modems in its AOLNet.
The company reported its earnings after markets closed. Earlier, its stock rose $3.875 to $51.25 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
